QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_18

question.text: For a close-ended Category III AIF, Incentive Fees are typically computed and payable:

answer.text: After completion of the fund tenure or at a 3-year cycle, as per the PPM

explanation.text: The Logic: For close-ended Category III AIFs, incentive fees are typically computed and payable after completion of the fund tenure, or mostly at a 3-year cycle/end of term, in order to avoid double-computation of excess return and to allow for future losses. The Trap: Options A and B would cause double-counting of profits during the fund's life. Option D is tied to capital drawdown, not to performance crystallisation. Note: The crystallisation timing applies to close-ended Category III AIFs as per the workbook's fee chapter.
